---
name: multi-category-sqlite-layout
description: "Layout, group-to-category mapping, join keys and price units of the 3-category product/review SQLite database"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 6943a139-f675-4581-b14a-097549b7b36e
  modified: 2026-10-01T17:25:11.354Z
---

Scope: the read-only SQLite database exposed by the `sql` query tool in this workspace, which bundles three per-category product datasets (office products, electronics, musical instruments). Observations below are from that database only.

Tables (12 + sqlite_sequence): `items_g1`, `items_g2`, `items_g3`; `fdbk_g1`, `fdbk_g2`, `fdbk_g3`; `taxn_g1`, `taxn_g2`; `attrs_g1`, `attrs_g3`; `fdbk_stats_g1`.

Group -> category mapping (INFERENCE, strongly supported by `main_cat` distributions over 20,000 items per group):
- g1 -> office products (13,933 `Office Products` items)
- g2 -> electronics (15,975 items in electronics categories: All Electronics / Camera & Photo / Cell Phones & Accessories / Car Electronics / Home Audio & Theater / Computers / Video Games)
- g3 -> musical instruments (17,162 `Musical Instruments` items)
No column in any table labels the group, so the mapping must be derived from `main_cat` counts, not read off directly.

Join keys (VERIFIED by join-coverage counts):
- `fdbk_g2.ref_id` -> `items_g2.ref_id` matches all 77,022 review rows.
- `fdbk_g2` also has an `item_id` column, but it matches `items_g2.ref_id` for only 49,393/77,022 rows, so `item_id` is NOT the reliable FK; use `ref_id`.
- `fdbk_g3` has no `item_id` column at all, so joins there can only use `ref_id`.

Price units in `items_g2` (VERIFIED over the 6,346 rows where both are non-null): `prc = prc_usd * 100` exactly (min and max ratio both 100.0). Thus `prc` is USD cents, `prc_usd` is USD dollars. Equality is verified only on the intersection of non-null rows, not on all rows. Because 6,570 prices exist in `prc` but only 6,346 in `prc_usd`, the two columns cannot be substituted in an arbitrary threshold or aggregate without checking coverage. Select the column covering the requested population and then convert units; do not silently discard a known price just because its converted column is NULL. 13,430 rows have NULL `prc` and 13,654 have NULL `prc_usd`.

Review fields: `fdbk_g*.rtg` is a real rating in [1,5] (so 1-star = `rtg = 1`); `fdbk_g*.body` is non-null in all 77,022 `fdbk_g2` rows; `fdbk_g2.ts` is an integer epoch (note `fdbk_g3.ts` is TEXT, a type difference between groups).

Schema varies between groups, so per-group SQL cannot be copy-pasted blindly: `items_g1`/`items_g3` carry `desc_txt` (and g1 also `avg_rtg_30d`, `rtg_ct`), `items_g2` carries `prc_usd`/`img_ct` but no `desc_txt`; `attrs_*` and `fdbk_stats_g1` exist for only some groups.

---
name: multi-category-sqlite-layout
description: "Layout, group-to-category mapping, join keys and price units of the 3-category product/review SQLite database"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 6943a139-f675-4581-b14a-097549b7b36e
  modified: 2026-10-01T17:25:11.354Z
---

Scope: the read-only SQLite database exposed by the `sql` query tool in this workspace, which bundles three per-category product datasets (office products, electronics, musical instruments). Observations below are from that database only.

Tables (12 + sqlite_sequence): `items_g1`, `items_g2`, `items_g3`; `fdbk_g1`, `fdbk_g2`, `fdbk_g3`; `taxn_g1`, `taxn_g2`; `attrs_g1`, `attrs_g3`; `fdbk_stats_g1`.

Group -> category mapping (INFERENCE, strongly supported by `main_cat` distributions over 20,000 items per group):
- g1 -> office products (13,933 `Office Products` items)
- g2 -> electronics (15,975 items in electronics categories: All Electronics / Camera & Photo / Cell Phones & Accessories / Car Electronics / Home Audio & Theater / Computers / Video Games)
- g3 -> musical instruments (17,162 `Musical Instruments` items)
No column in any table labels the group, so the mapping must be derived from `main_cat` counts, not read off directly.

Join keys (VERIFIED by join-coverage counts):
- `fdbk_g2.ref_id` -> `items_g2.ref_id` matches all 77,022 review rows.
- `fdbk_g2` also has an `item_id` column, but it matches `items_g2.ref_id` for only 49,393/77,022 rows, so `item_id` is NOT the reliable FK; use `ref_id`.
- `fdbk_g3` has no `item_id` column at all, so joins there can only use `ref_id`.

Price units in `items_g2` (VERIFIED over the 6,346 rows where both are non-null): `prc = prc_usd * 100` exactly (min and max ratio both 100.0). Thus `prc` is USD cents, `prc_usd` is USD dollars. Equality is verified only on the intersection of non-null rows, not on all rows. Because 6,570 prices exist in `prc` but only 6,346 in `prc_usd`, the two columns cannot be substituted in an arbitrary threshold or aggregate without checking coverage. Select the column covering the requested population and then convert units; do not silently discard a known price just because its converted column is NULL. 13,430 rows have NULL `prc` and 13,654 have NULL `prc_usd`.

Review fields: `fdbk_g*.rtg` is a real rating in [1,5] (so 1-star = `rtg = 1`); `fdbk_g*.body` is non-null in all 77,022 `fdbk_g2` rows; `fdbk_g2.ts` is an integer epoch (note `fdbk_g3.ts` is TEXT, a type difference between groups).

Schema varies between groups, so per-group SQL cannot be copy-pasted blindly: `items_g1`/`items_g3` carry `desc_txt` (and g1 also `avg_rtg_30d`, `rtg_ct`), `items_g2` carries `prc_usd`/`img_ct` but no `desc_txt`; `attrs_*` and `fdbk_stats_g1` exist for only some groups.

content.text:
## Findings

**Which tables are electronics:** `items_g2` is the electronics dataset — its `main_cat` distribution is dominated by electronics categories (Computers 5,247, All Electronics 4,562, Camera & Photo 2,789, Cell Phones & Accessories 1,775, Home Audio & Theater 1,248, Car Electronics 346, Video Games 8). Group mapping: g1 = office, g2 = electronics, g3 = musical instruments.

**Schema:** `items_g2(ref_id, ttl, avg_rtg, prc INTEGER, prc_usd REAL, str_nm, main_cat, feat_lst, img_ct)`.

**Price units (verified, not assumed):** on all 6,346 rows where both columns are non-null, `prc / prc_usd` ranges from 99.99999999999999 to 100.00000000000001 → `prc` is USD **cents**, `prc_usd` is dollars.

**The coverage trap:** `prc` is non-null for 6,570 rows but `prc_usd` for only 6,346 — and there are **zero** rows with `prc_usd` but no `prc`. So the correct population is the 6,570 `prc` rows. The 224 `prc`-only rows are high-end products (a $26,888 security robot, $4,868 SunBrite TV, Leica/Nikon pro lenses), which is why the two candidate queries diverge sharply:

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| `AVG(prc_usd)` (6,346 rows — drops the expensive tail) | **$52.96** |
| `AVG(prc)/100` over all 6,570 priced rows | **$96.23** |

Answer: **$96.23** (for reference, restricting to electronics `main_cat`s only gives $97.97; no zero/negative prices exist).

```json
{
  "answer": "96.23",
  "sql": "SELECT AVG(COALESCE(prc / 100.0, prc_usd)) AS avg_listed_price_usd, COUNT(COALESCE(prc / 100.0, prc_usd)) AS n_priced FROM items_g2;"
}
```

💡 I updated the existing `environment.md` memory with the coverage skew (224 high-end `prc`-only rows; union = `prc` rows since no `prc_usd`-only rows exist) and the ~45% understatement from aggregating `prc_usd` alone.
